screen.title: Install what is missing
screen.intro: Based on the environment check, these components still need to be installed. Each one shows exactly what it is about to do and waits for your confirmation before starting.
screen.nothingNeededHint: Nothing to do in this step — go straight on to the configuration.
screen.noSnapshot: There is no environment check result yet. Please go back to “Environment” and run it first.
screen.allDone: Every item in this step is handled. You can move on.
screen.pendingHint: Finish or skip each item above before continuing.
screen.navigationLocked: An install or download is running — wait for it to finish (or cancel it) before leaving this step.

plan.generic: {{tool}} will be installed as shown below.
plan.npm_global: {{tool}} will be installed with npm into the current user's global folder. The output of the install is shown live below.

node.download_page: Node.js is installed from the official installer. Use the button below to open the download page, download the “LTS” installer (Windows: .msi, macOS: .pkg) and click through it with the defaults.
node.homebrew: Homebrew was detected, so Node.js can also be installed by running the command below in a terminal (open a new terminal window afterwards; if node is still not found, run brew link --overwrite node once); or simply install it from the download page below.
node.msi: Runs the Node.js installer you just downloaded as administrator (msiexec, unattended with the default options). Windows shows a User Account Control prompt — click “Yes”. The check re-runs automatically afterwards.
node.pkg: Runs the Node.js package you just downloaded (macOS installer). macOS asks for your password to grant administrator rights; the install starts once you enter it. The check re-runs automatically afterwards.

cc_switch.download: CC Switch is a desktop app. The installer is downloaded from the official release channel, its integrity is verified, and then you run it yourself.

codex_app.msix: Installs the offline package you just downloaded with PowerShell's Add-AppxPackage (for the current user only, no administrator rights). The check re-runs automatically afterwards.
codex_app.dmg: Mounts the downloaded image, copies the app into the Applications folder and ejects the image. No administrator rights needed; the check re-runs automatically afterwards.
codex_app.download: The Codex desktop client ships inside the ChatGPT desktop app. Open the download page, install it, then come back and re-check.

actions.installerBlocked: The installer was blocked or does not open

common.commandHint: Nothing runs until you click “Confirm and run”; this tool never runs commands silently as administrator.

requiresAdmin.title: The npm global folder needs administrator rights
requiresAdmin.body: npm's global install folder is not writable for your account, so running the command as-is will most likely fail. This tool will not elevate for you and will not change your npm configuration. Pick one of these:
requiresAdmin.optionElevated: Open a terminal as administrator (Windows: right-click “Windows Terminal” → “Run as administrator”; macOS: prefix the command with sudo) and run the command above by hand.
requiresAdmin.optionPrefix: Move npm's global folder into your own user folder (recommended — no administrator rights needed afterwards). Run this in a terminal yourself:
requiresAdmin.prefixHint: Afterwards add that folder (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.npm-global; macOS: $HOME/.npm-global/bin) to your PATH and open a new terminal. Step-by-step guide in the npm docs:
requiresAdmin.docsLabel: npm docs: resolving global install permission errors

common.commandHintInstaller: Nothing runs until you click “Install now”; the operating system shows its usual authorisation prompt — this tool never elevates silently.

npm.successHint: The install command succeeded. Re-checking that the tool is available…
npm.failedHint: The install command failed (exit code {{code}}). Check the output above; for network timeouts or download errors, switch the registry and retry.
npm.failedNoCode: The install command did not finish normally. Check the output above and retry.
npm.timedOut: The install command was stopped after {{minutes}} min without finishing. Usually the registry is slow or blocked from this network: switch the registry and retry, or check VPN / proxy settings.
npm.startFailed: The install command could not be started.
npm.recheckStillMissing: The install command succeeded, but the re-check still cannot find the command. Usually the terminal PATH has not refreshed yet: close every terminal window completely, reopen, then re-check from the “Environment” step.

steps.title: Steps
steps.open: Click “Open download page” and download the “LTS” (long-term support) installer.
steps.run: Run the installer and click through it with the default options.
steps.close: When it finishes, close every terminal window that is already open (only new terminals will see node).
steps.recheck: Come back here and click “I installed it — re-check”.

node.recheckNotPassed: Re-check result: {{message}}. If you only just installed it, close every terminal window completely (or sign out and back in) and re-check again.

oneClick.intro: This tool downloads the Node.js LTS installer from the source below, verifies its SHA-256 and then — after your confirmation — runs the installer.
oneClick.sourceChosen: The network probe picked: {{source}} (chosen automatically by reachability and speed)
oneClick.adminAhead: Running the installer needs administrator rights: the system will show an authorisation prompt.
oneClick.fetchFailed: Could not fetch the Node.js installer information (network or mirror unreachable). Use the manual path below for now.

ccSwitch.intro: CC Switch is the desktop app used to configure and switch providers. This tool fetches the latest version from the official release channel, verifies the file after download and hands it over to you to install.
ccSwitch.fetchFailed: Could not fetch the CC Switch release information. You can also open the release page and download it by hand.
ccSwitch.blockedNote: Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper may block an installer it does not recognise. Follow the steps below, then run the installer again.

afterDownload.title: Next
afterDownload.open: Click “Open installer” to run it (or double-click the file at the location above).
afterDownload.windows: On Windows, if “Windows protected your PC” appears, click “More info” → “Run anyway”; choose “Install for me only” — no administrator rights needed.
afterDownload.macos: On macOS, if it refuses to open, right-click the app in Finder and choose “Open”, or go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”.
afterDownload.recheck: When the install finishes, come back here and click “I installed it — re-check”.

ccSwitch.recheckNotPassed: Re-check result: {{message}}. Make sure the installer has finished, then try again.

recheck.failed: The re-check failed; you can try again later from the “Environment” step.

skip.warning: Skipped installing {{tool}}. Later configuration or verification steps may fail because of it; you can come back to this step at any time.

download.unverified: Not verified (the publisher provided no hash)
download.verifiedFalse: Verification failed — do not run this file

adminNote: The system will show an administrator authorisation / password prompt; this tool never elevates silently.

oneClick.waitingForPrompt: If a User Account Control or password prompt appears, confirm it there; the progress is shown below.

release.hashAvailable: SHA-256 provided; verified automatically after download
release.hashMissing: This release ships no SHA-256, so it cannot be verified automatically; make sure the source is the official channel

installer.successHint: The installer finished. Re-checking that the tool is available…
installer.planFailed: Could not build the command that runs the installer. You can open the installer yourself and re-check afterwards.
installer.downloadFailed: The download failed. Check the network and retry, or use the manual path below.
installer.failedHint: The installer failed (exit code {{code}}). Check the output above; if you dismissed the authorisation prompt, simply try again.
installer.failedNoCode: The installer did not finish normally. Check the output above and retry.
installer.timedOut: The installer was stopped after {{minutes}} min without finishing. Retry, or open the installer yourself.
installer.startFailed: The installer could not be started.

codexApp.title: Codex desktop client
codexApp.intro: The Codex desktop client ships inside the ChatGPT desktop app. Optional but recommended: it adds a graphical interface and “Sign in with ChatGPT”. The Codex CLI works without it.

actions.downloadOffline: Download the offline package and install

region.title: Does the Store say it is not available in your region?
region.body: The Microsoft Store decides by the system region whether an app is visible. Temporarily switch the region (e.g. United States) and reopen the Store — or simply use “Download the offline package and install” above.
region.step1: Click “Open region settings” (Settings → Time & language → Region).
region.step3: Close the Microsoft Store completely, reopen it and search for Codex / ChatGPT again.

afterDownload.windows: After the download the install command is shown (Add-AppxPackage, current user only, no administrator rights) and runs once you confirm.
afterDownload.macos: After the download the install command is shown: mount the image, copy the app into Applications, eject the image. No administrator rights needed.

codexApp.fetchFailed: Could not resolve the Codex desktop client download. You can open the download page and install it by hand.
codexApp.recheckNotPassed: Re-check result: {{message}}. Make sure the install has finished (a Store install can take a minute or two), then try again.
